title: Prowell Governor & Performance Parameters
subtitle: This week covers the loaded (gravity) governor analysis in detail, then finishes with the 6 key performance parameters every governor is judged on. These parameters are definition-heavy — expect them in exams.
learningOutcome: This week covers the loaded (gravity) governor analysis in detail, then finishes with the 6 key performance parameters every governor is judged on. These parameters are definition-heavy — expect them in exams.

content.text: Definition: The ability of the governor to maintain constant speed of rotation. Can be obtained mathematically as the ratio (N_max − N_min)/N_min.

items: A governor is stable when for each speed within the working range, there is only one radius of the governor balls at which the governor is in equilibrium.
A governor is said to be isochronous when the equilibrium speed is constant for all radii of rotation within the working range.
Hunting is a condition in which the speed of the engine controlled by the governor fluctuates continuously above and below the mean speed.
The effort of a governor is the force it can exert at the sleeve on the mechanism which controls the supply of fuel to the engine.
Power is defined as the work done at the sleeve for a given percentage change of speed.

content.text: Common mistake — Confusing isochronism and stability. An isochronous governor has ONE equilibrium speed for ALL radii — this means it is infinitely sensitive, which actually makes it unstable (prone to hunting). Stable ≠ isochronous.
